what: Every economic effect of the value-bearing ZK and privacy products of the delivery plan: its class, handler, the ledger invariants checked independently of the proof verifier with their enforcement sites, the authorized source of issued units, what stays exposed when a proof is accepted wrongly, and the tests that mutate it. Per protocol: how retained state stays readable, how an effect is cancelled or expires, how a failure rolls back, and how assets leave under key or policy revocation and correction. Root publication and history policy, with every suspension switch found. `--show` prints one line per effect, `--defects` one per open defect.
not_a_soundness_claim: A ledger invariant recorded here says what the ledger refuses or bounds when a proof is accepted wrongly. It is never evidence that a proof relation is sound, that hidden value is conserved, or that an individual depositor is protected: a reserve balance bounds what can leave a pool and says nothing about what is inside it. `enforced` means the named site exists and the named test mutates it; it does not mean the invariant is sufficient. Nothing here states readiness, qualification or deployment.

addressed.note: Each value-bearing protocol answers retained-state readability, cancellation or expiry, failure atomicity and exits under key revocation, policy revocation and correction, with a site or an open defect. Root publication and history are recorded with their committed policy; the suspension switches the requirement forbids are recorded as open defects with their owners.

The matrix records which pools have a public reserve today (Orchard and private-IVM, the closed list of the source), that FCMP++, PQ-MASP, Anonymous PGC and settlement pools are closed with no transparent exit, and what bounds the exposure of each. The parts of the finding that are not built are open defects: no turnstile or cap, unbacked genesis notes, unbounded genesis sets, confidential assets without value instructions. The added tests show that a withdrawal forced past verification cannot exceed the reserve and that reserves are exclusive across pools.

ledger_effects.what: Every class of ledger effect the one verifier returns, with the arm of the proof handler that applies it. A class recorded as moving no value lists identifiers its arm must not name.

reserve_owners.what: The pools that may own a public reserve. A protocol outside this list has no transparent exit.

pool_state.what: Every committed World map that holds pool, nullifier, commitment or root state, with the protocols that own it. A map that appears under these names without an entry fails the check, so another shielded pool cannot enter the tree unrecorded.

root_policy.statement: Roots that carry value are proof-managed: they are created by a typed bootstrap and advanced only by a verified action or a certified settlement leg of their pool; governance cannot publish, advance or rewrite them. History length is a committed parameter. No instruction suspends publication or history of one pool. The plan requires that no generic suspension switch controls them; the tree has the switches recorded below, each an open defect.

publication.statement: Generic publication serves governance-managed roles only. A proof-managed role, a PGC account-state root, an account-registry root and every X.509 root are refused; a governance-managed root must advance its epoch and its head must agree with retained history.

history.statement: The number of retained roots per namespace and role is `retained_root_count` of the committed privacy consensus policy, and the lower pending value while a tightening is scheduled. A successor root is added and the oldest retained roots are removed in the same transaction, per namespace; a replayed, conflicting, stale or over-capacity root is refused. A statement anchored outside the retained window is refused. Settlement roots are kept with their provenance and a duplicate pool epoch is refused at restore. A governance-managed history that is full refuses a further publication instead of pruning, because no typed anchor-chain validator exists for those roles.

defects.summary: The governance instruction TransitionPrivacyProtocolLifecycleV1 moves a registered protocol to Suspended or Retired. Every proof of that protocol is then refused, including an Orchard unshield and a private-IVM withdrawal, and Retired is terminal. A pool reserve can be debited only by a verified proof of its pool, so value shielded in a pool has no exit while its protocol is suspended and none at all after retirement.
defects.required: Remove the lifecycle availability switch (plan, 'Runtime validity without activation gates'). A relation that must be corrected is replaced by an ordinary signed deployment with a defined exit for existing notes.

defects.summary: A registered protocol starts in Proposed and its effects, pool bootstraps and generic root publication are refused until an explicit activation transition and the all-twelve qualification record exist.
defects.required: Registration of a supported canonical profile creates usable state; remove the activation step and the qualification record (P.5).

defects.symbol: "cannot publish a root for a retired privacy protocol"
defects.summary: Generic root publication reads the protocol lifecycle: a root of a retired protocol cannot be published, and a proof-managed root cannot advance while its protocol is not Active because only a proof advances it.
defects.required: Root publication and history follow the committed root policy alone; remove the lifecycle read with the lifecycle itself (P.5).

defects.summary: Every settlement instruction first requires the node-configured atomic-settlement switch, its activation height and notice period, and an Active private-IVM protocol activation. Turning either off stops pool activation, prepare, finalize and abort for every pool.
defects.required: Atomic settlement is usable when its relation and keys are committed; remove the node-configured switch and the activation read (P.5, P.20).

defects.summary: A settlement pool policy can carry a retirement height. A bundle that expires at or after it is refused, and settlement pools have no transparent boundary, so notes of a retired pool can neither move nor leave.
defects.required: Define how notes leave a pool whose policy is retired or replaced: a successor pool reachable by a settlement leg, or an explicit withdrawal with its own ledger invariant.

defects.summary: A pool is bound to the compiled profile of the binary: its activation carries the parameter, verifier, statement schema and engine manifest digests, and a proof is admitted only against that exact profile. When a relation is corrected those digests change. No instruction migrates the notes of an existing pool or releases its reserve under the replaced relation.
defects.required: State the correction path per pool with T.1's cutover: either a fresh-genesis cutover that says what happens to pool reserves, or a governed exit instruction with an independent ledger invariant.

defects.summary: Orchard and private-IVM pools keep no committed counter of cumulative deposits and withdrawals and no committed supply cap. The reserve balance is the only bound on withdrawals, and ordinary transfers into the reserve raise it.
defects.required: P.16 requires an exact per-pool turnstile and explicitly committed supply or issuance caps; P.2 enforces them as ordinary committed transaction rules.

defects.summary: A private-IVM pool is bootstrapped with a non-empty set of genesis note commitments chosen by governance. Their hidden value is matched by no reserve deposit and consumes no committed allowance, although the pool has a transparent exit. A genesis note can be withdrawn only from units that deposits or ordinary transfers put into the reserve, so it is paid by other depositors.
defects.required: Shielded value seeded at bootstrap is matched by an equal reserve deposit when the pool is admitted, or the genesis set carries a committed public amount (finding R6-22, item 2).

defects.summary: The whole supply of an FCMP++ pool is the hidden value of the genesis outputs governance supplies at bootstrap. No public figure, committed allowance or backing asset movement bounds it.
defects.required: State the issuance source of the pool: a committed public supply figure the bootstrap is checked against, or a funded bridge with its own invariant (plan: an added bridge requires explicit economics).

defects.summary: The whole supply of a PQ-MASP pool is the hidden value of the genesis note commitments governance supplies at bootstrap. No public figure, committed allowance or backing asset movement bounds it.
defects.required: State the issuance source of the pool: a committed public supply figure the bootstrap is checked against, or a funded bridge with its own invariant.

defects.summary: The total supply of an Anonymous PGC pool is a public number governance chooses at bootstrap. It is bound to no asset definition and consumes no committed issuance allowance; the bootstrap proof is the only check that the encrypted balances sum to it.
defects.required: Name what a PGC unit is: bind the pool to an asset and a committed allowance, or state that the units are pool-local with no claim on any asset.

defects.summary: A settlement pool is activated with initial commitments chosen by governance. Their hidden value is bound only by an opaque asset-binding commitment; no public figure or committed allowance bounds it.
defects.required: State the issuance source of a settlement pool and how its initial commitments are funded.

defects.summary: The ledger finalizes a settlement from committee certificates. The leg proofs, and with them conservation inside a leg and across the legs of a bundle, are checked only by the committee validators off the instruction path; the carrier omits the proofs. Nothing on the ledger relates the value leaving one pool to the value entering another.
defects.required: P.20 puts spend authorization and conservation in a relation the ledger verifies, or P.2 names the public quantity that is conserved across legs.

defects.summary: The checks the proof handler applies to a verified effect (Orchard, FCMP++, Anonymous PGC, ZK-ACE) are inline after the one verifier call, and so are the checks of the PGC bootstrap handler after its own verifier call. No entry point takes a verified effect, so a test cannot apply the effect a faulty verifier would return and observe those checks. Only the public reserve bridge and the private-note apply function are reachable that way today.
defects.required: Split the handler into verification and an apply function over the verified effect (the single state executor per role of P.1), and give every ledger effect a test-only constructor like the proof-managed one (P.3).

defects.summary: A ZK-ACE policy names an asset and a list of source accounts and no amount. A proof accepted under it moves any amount the named source holds, with no signature of the source.
defects.required: P.15 decides whether a policy carries a committed allowance; P.2 enforces it if it does.

defects.summary: Confidential assets have committed pool state (commitments, nullifiers, root history, an unshield key binding) and policy modes, and no shield, transfer or unshield instruction: nothing in the tree appends a commitment or consumes a nullifier of this pool outside tests.
defects.required: P.9 delivers the three instructions with amount, authority and conservation effects, and a per-asset public reserve or supply ledger so that cumulative unshields cannot exceed shields (finding R6-22, item 1).

defects.summary: The ledger reservation of the two replay identities of an anchored spend (issuer nonce and source transfer) exists with its own test (`anchored_axt_source_transfer_replay_is_cross_envelope_and_atomic`, written through the `state_test!` macro), and nothing calls it: an envelope that carries a spend is refused before any proof is read.
defects.required: A.1 binds the finalized source and the current issuer; A.3 delivers the spend with its replay reservation, issuer budget and exact effective amount.

defects.required: A test that registers allocations up to and one over the vault balance, and a test-only entry after the verifier so the check can be shown with verification forced to succeed.

defects.summary: The lease-conflict and capacity checks of a fee-sponsor allocation run after the FASTPQ verifier call inside one handler. No test-only entry applies an allocation with verification forced to succeed, and the accepting tests need a real FASTPQ AXT proof (about 48 minutes in a debug build).
defects.required: Split the handler into verification and an apply function over the verified claim so the capacity bound can be shown independently of the proof.

defects.summary: No test settles a game session with a proof, real or forced. Staked sessions are refused at open while the compiled profile is unqualified, so only unfunded sessions settle today.
defects.required: B.3 delivers the RaceV1 relation on the shared backend with settlement tests, including a forced-success verifier showing that a wrong outcome pays at most the session liability.

defects.summary: A ZK ballot is refused before any proof is dispatched, so its bond lock cannot run.
defects.required: P.8 delivers the ballot relation; the bond lock stays the exact transfer into escrow the plain ballot uses.
